newsitem.title: UK: EMI restructures American music business.
newsitem.headline: EMI restructures American music business.

text.p: Britain's EMI Group Plc is restructuring its North American music operations and has taken a 117.2 million pound ($191.9 million) charge to cover the cost, the company said on Tuesday.

EMI, one of the world's five major music companies, also said it had agreed in principle to return capital to shareholders. It said this could be in the order of 10 percent of the group's current market value.
EMI reported pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit of 380.5 million pounds in the year to end-March, a 3.6 percent rise.
The company said progress in the current year was likely to be modest, citing the strength of sterling and subdued industry conditions.

EMI Music plans to streamline the management of its North American operations, to integrate them more closely with the management of its international business and resolve issues relating to the North American music retail industry.

Ken Berry, now head of EMI Music International and Virgin Records, will become president of EMI Recorded Music embracing EMI Music International, EMI Capitol and Virgin. He will continue to report to Jim Fifield, CEO of EMI Music.
The restructuring is expected to result in annual savings of 35-40 million pounds in operating costs, with slightly less than half of that amount arising in the current financial year.

EMI said it hoped to have proposals for the return of capital available for consideration by shareholders at the time of its annual meeting on July 18 and implement them shortly afterwards. EMI's current market capitalisation is around 5.3 billion pounds.($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
